stem:
Hemant studies the diagram of square $ABCD$. Dashed segment $AC$ is a diagonal. Grey points $W$, $X$, $Y$, $Z$ are the midpoints of the sides, joined to form square $WXYZ$.

One or more options may be correct. Which two claims are correct?

options.text: Build a new square on diagonal $AC$ to double the area of $ABCD$.
Join midpoints $W$, $X$, $Y$, $Z$ to form square $WXYZ$ and halve the area of $ABCD$.
Join the midpoints to double the area, and build on diagonal $AC$ to halve it.
Treat every inscribed quadrilateral inside $ABCD$ as a half-area square.

teacher.key_rationale: A square on the diagonal of ABCD has twice the area; the midpoint square WXYZ has half the area. Reversing those roles, or treating every inscribed quadrilateral as half-area, is wrong.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source grid quadrilateral as square ABCD with dashed diagonal AC and midpoint square WXYZ.
